items.anchor: This appendix constructs the planar comparison vector field
items.note: The field of Lemma art:planar-field (planar_field), used in the proof of Theorem art:planar-cluster (A/local/proof/005).

items.title: Planar contour comparison field
items.note: planar_field states the lemma with its hypotheses written out (module docstring): F convex (hF); F_* the minimum (IsLeast (range F) Fstar); C nonempty, compact, C ⊆ {F = ℓ}, ℓ > F_*; no nontrivial segment in frontier {F ≤ ℓ} (hstrict); no affine-critical point in C (IsAffineCritical F p is 0 ∈ aff ∂F(p), see isAffineCritical_iff); and hregular, the smooth or regular convex two-branch structure of hypothesis 2 of Theorem art:planar-cluster written as in the TeX and in the coverage of local.tex (F C² on an open V ∋ p, or F = max{f₁, f₂} on an open V ∋ p with f₁, f₂ convex and C² on V, both active at p, ∇f₁(p), ∇f₂(p) linearly independent); regularity_of_literal and literal_of_regularity show it is equivalent to the library's ContDiffAt ℝ 2 F p ∨ ConvexTwoBranchRegularAt F p; 0 < c₁ < c₂ < 1. Conclusion: ∃ U Q w η κ δ C₀ C₁ L, all before the pair (the quantifier order of the last sentence), with U open ⊇ C, Q compact ⊇ closure U, η, κ, δ > 0, C₀, C₁, L ≥ 0. Item 1: 'w defined on a neighborhood of Q and locally Lipschitz' is: w is locally Lipschitz at every point of an open N ⊇ Q (w is a total function); ‖w‖ ≤ B on Q (Euclidean); η ≤ gᵀw(p) and equal pairings for all g ∈ ∂F(p), p ∈ Q. Items 2 and 3 for every eligible pair x, z ∈ U (EligiblePair F c₁ c₂ x z g h: g, h the gradients at x, z, d > 0, c₁d ≤ Δ ≤ d, t ≥ (1-c₂)d, as in Lemma art:planar-field) with ‖s‖ < δ, where s = z - x, y = h - g, d = -gᵀs = -dot g (z - x), t = yᵀs = dot (h - g) (z - x) are written out and det(s,·) is pairDet s ·. Proof: the library's PlanarAllPairs.source_all_endpoint_estimates (same construction as the TeX proof; its field is PlanarObjectiveField.field hF χ v), with N from PlanarObjectiveField.exists_open_local_lipschitz_extension and the bound on Q from continuity on the compact Q. The hypotheses that F attains F_*, C ≠ ∅, ℓ > F_* and c₁ < c₂ are not needed by the proof (prefixed _); they are kept because the lemma states them.

planar_field is proved along this proof. The steps that were displays before M45 and are now inline are stated in smooth_pairing (grad F(x)^Tw(x) = ||grad F(x)|| h > 0), log_determinant_derivative_bound (|H_+'| <= A(phi_+' + 2d)), comparison_functions and log_determinant_increment (|H(1)-H(0)| <= 2Ad), crossing_numerator (|y^Tw(z)| <= A_1||s||) and crossing_pairings (the two pairing identities).

Stated at a nonsmooth point c ∈ C with the two-branch data of hregular at c as variables (open V ∋ c, branches f₁, f₂ convex and C² on V, F = max{f₁, f₂} on V, both active at c, independent gradients), the curve p_j as a variable p with its characterization (p ℓ = c, C² at ℓ, f₁(p(t)) = f₂(p(t)) = t for t near ℓ) and v = deriv p. Conclusion: v is C¹ at ℓ (the 'C¹ velocity') and both pairings equal 1 for t near ℓ. corner_curve proves the preceding claims (the branch-value map x ↦ (f₁(x), f₂(x)) has an invertible derivative at c; the inverse function theorem gives such a C² curve, which near c is the only point where f₁ = f₂), so the assumptions on p can be met.

height χ v t θ is literally the display, for angular cutoffs χ : Fin m → ℝ → ℝ and velocities v : Fin m → ℝ → Vec 2, with n(θ) = normal θ = (cos θ, sin θ). In the Lean construction the angular cutoffs are θ ↦ χ_j(n(θ)) for smooth ambient cutoffs χ_j : ℝ² → ℝ (so they are smooth and 2π-periodic); height_eq_library identifies height with the library's PlanarJoinedFrame.height and PlanarAmbientFrame.height for them.

fieldFormula χ v t θ = h(t,θ)n(θ) + h_θ(t,θ)T(θ) with h_θ = deriv (height χ v t), so the display is w(x) = fieldFormula χ v (F x) θ(x), where θ(x) is any angle with n(θ(x)) = ∇F(x)/‖∇F(x)‖ (exists_angle: such an angle exists when ∇F(x) ≠ 0; fieldFormula_periodic: the formula is 2π-periodic). field_eq_fieldFormula is the unfolding theorem for the field of the Lean proof, PlanarObjectiveField.field hF χ v (ambient form of the formula at a selected subgradient's unit normal): at every point where F has gradient g, and every θ with n(θ) = g/‖g‖, it equals the displayed formula with the angular cutoffs θ ↦ χ_j(n(θ)).

corner_field_formula is the calculation 'h = nᵀv_j, h_θ = Tᵀv_j, w(x) = v_j(F(x))' at a smooth point whose normal angle has a neighborhood on which χ_j = 1 (the other cutoffs then vanish there, by disjoint supports). corner_field is the neighborhood statement for the field of the proof, at a corner c with its two-branch data and curve as in disp/003: if the ambient cutoff χ_j equals 1 on a neighborhood of the normal arc at c (normalSector of ∇f₁(c), ∇f₂(c), the unit directions of their cone), then near c every subgradient is nonzero with unit normal in the plateau, and w(z) = v_j(F(z)) for all z near c, on both smooth sides and on the switching curve (the formula is used on the curve itself).

For C² angular cutoffs, any velocities and any level t, with h = height χ v t (a variable with its definition): the derivative of θ ↦ h(θ)n(θ) + h'(θ)T(θ) at θ is (h(θ) + h''(θ))T(θ). No sign or convexity condition on h.

derivative_triangular: at a point x where F is C² with ∇F(x) ≠ 0, the velocities are C¹ at F(x), and w is given by (art:planar-field-formula) near x (for every angle of the normal), w is differentiable at x, Dw = fderiv ℝ w x maps the tangent line {u : nᵀu = 0} into itself, and with n = ∇F(x)/‖∇F(x)‖, T = rotate n (= T(θ(x))), a = TᵀDwT, b = TᵀDw n, e = nᵀDw n: Dw T = aT and Dw n = bT + en, i.e. the matrix of Dw in the basis (T,n) is [[a,b],[0,e]]. derivative_coefficients_bounded is 'with bounded coefficients': if w is locally Lipschitz on an open N containing the compact buffer Q, one B bounds |a|, |b|, |e| at every point of Q for every unit normal n.

The display is inside a proof by contradiction. transversality_limits states it for sequences x_k, z_k, g_k, h_k with s_k = z_k - x_k → 0, x_k → p ∈ Q, s_k/‖s_k‖ → ŝ, g_k → ḡ, h_k → h̄, ḡ, h̄ ∈ ∂F(p) and ŝ = -w(p)/‖w(p)‖ (the facts derived before the display), d_k = -g_kᵀs_k, t_k = (h_k - g_k)ᵀs_k, with visibility η > 0 and common pairing of w on Q. It does not assume that the pairs are eligible: with eligibility these assumptions are contradictory, which is what the next sentence uses (transversality_contradiction derives False from them). Lean names gbar, hbar, shat. Without eligibility the assumptions are satisfiable: an example at the end of the module gives constant sequences at the smooth point (1/20, 0) of the objective of Theorem art:nonradial-example.

At a segment point q = x + θs of an eligible pair where F is C² with ∇F(q) ≠ 0 and w is given by the formula near q, with n, T, a, b, e as in disp/008 at q and s_T = Tᵀs, s_n = nᵀs: det(T,n) = -1, s = s_T T + s_n n, and det(s, Dw s) = s_n((a - e)s_T + b s_n). det(u,v) is pairDet u v = u₀v₁ - u₁v₀ (columns u, v); the sign is the TeX's.

The larger convex chart is an open convex V on which f is convex and C^2 with grad f M-Lipschitz (Euclidean norm, M > 0). The first inequality is branch_cocoercivity; the second, D_f(z,x) <= t, holds since t = D_f(z,x) + D_f(x,z) and D_f(x,z) >= 0 (same_branch_secant gives ||y||^2 <= 2Mt).

'Their inverse bound' is A₂ ≥ 0 with ‖u‖ ≤ A₂(|∇f₀(x')ᵀu| + |∇f₁(x')ᵀu|) for all u and all x' in the chart (Euclidean ‖u‖); its existence near a corner is the library's eventually_actual_pair_control (sup norm, which differs from the Euclidean norm by at most a factor 2). Both displayed inequalities are proved. crossing_secant proves the next sentences (lines 168-170): if A₂ > 0 and A₂M‖s‖ ≤ 1/2, then t ≥ a₀‖s‖ with a₀ = 1/(2A₂(1 + 2/(1 - c₂))) > 0 and (yᵀw(z))²/t ≤ A₁²‖s‖/a₀.
